passages.context: Gregory first insists that the preacher must hear and do God's words before speaking them. He then reads Mark 7:32-35 spiritually: Christ's fingers signify the gifts of the Holy Spirit opening the deaf heart to obedience; saliva signifies wisdom received from Christ's mouth and forms the tongue for preaching; Christ's upward look and sigh teach prayer; and right speech follows obedient action.
passages.notes: Verified word for word against the page image of Migne's printing, with the keyed web transcription used only as a discovery and comparison witness. The passage is at PL 76:893-894; bold 1270-1271 in the body is Maurist-source pagination and must not be cited as PL columns. This passage supports Gregory's reception of Mark 7 and does not by itself establish the historical intention of any later missal compiler.

work.author: Gregory the Great
work.description: Gregory the Great's two books of homilies on Ezekiel, including the treatment in book I, homily 10, section 20 of Christ's healing of the deaf man in Mark 7:32-35 as an opening of the heart to obedience and of the tongue to preaching.
